forestsearch

Interpretable subgroup identification in randomized clinical trials, with post-selection inference for the effect the trial reports.

forestsearch identifies a subgroup defined by explicit covariate cuts, such as “no measured estrogen receptor and progesterone receptor at most 26 fmol/l”. It reports the trial’s standard analysis for that subgroup and for the patients outside it, corrected for the selection that produced the subgroup. Survival outcomes use the Cox hazard ratio. Binary, continuous and count outcomes use the coefficient of a generalized linear model: an odds ratio, relative risk, risk difference, mean difference or incidence-rate ratio.

The methods are described in León and Anderson (2026a, 2026b), and in León et al. (2024) for the original procedure (see Citation below).

How it works

  1. Candidates. The search enumerates every conjunction of at most two covariate cuts (maxk = 2) that meets minimum size and event counts. The candidates come from the covariates alone; no outcome model decides them.
  2. Screen. Each candidate receives the trial’s own analysis within the subgroup. A candidate is admitted when its effect clears the screening threshold and its splitting-consistency rate reaches p*. The rate is the probability that both halves of a random half-split clear the consistency threshold, and it is evaluated in closed form from one fit (consistency_method = "resample", the default).
  3. Select. A stated rule chooses among the admitted candidates. For example, sg_focus = "effMaxSG" with effect_neighborhood = 0.20 takes the largest subgroup whose effect is within 20% of the strongest. The search can also return no subgroup.
  4. Correct. With mr_inference = TRUE, multiplier resampling re-applies the selection rule to jointly perturbed candidate effects, without refitting. It reports a de-biased estimate for the subgroup and for its complement, a one-sided selection-adjusted bound for each, and a Bonferroni pair for a joint claim on both.
  5. Calibrate. fs_declaration_calibration() estimates how often the screen, as run, would declare a subgroup if every patient benefited by a clinically specified amount. It also gives the cutoff that would hold that rate at a nominal level.

Model-based identifiers can propose the candidates instead: DINA (subgroup_method = "dina") and causal forests (subgroup_method = "grf"). Their regions are re-ranked on the same coefficient and receive the same inference, conditional on the candidate family they propose. The full bootstrap correction and the cross-validation of León et al. (2024) remain available.

Bounds are read by where they lie against the trial’s own effect and against clinically meaningful effect sizes, not as tests at a hazard ratio of one.

Installation

From CRAN:

install.packages("forestsearch")

The development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("larry-leon/forestsearch")

Quick start

This is the forest-search analysis of the German Breast Cancer Study Group trial in Table 1 of León and Anderson (2026b). vignette("forestsearch") runs it in full, with the two model-based identifiers, and reads every number.

library(forestsearch)
library(survival)

df <- within(gbsg, {
  id          <- seq_len(nrow(gbsg))
  time_months <- rfstime / 30.4375
  grade3      <- ifelse(grade == "3", 1, 0)
})

fit <- forestsearch(
  df.analysis = df,
  outcome.name = "time_months", event.name = "status",
  treat.name = "hormon", id.name = "id",
  confounders.name = c("age", "meno", "size", "grade3", "nodes", "pgr", "er"),
  is.RCT = TRUE, est.scale = "hr", seedit = 8316951,
  # the candidate family
  conf.cont_jcuts = list(er = 10, pgr = 10), conf_force = c("er <= 0", "pgr <= 0"),
  n.min = 60, d0.min = 10, d1.min = 10, maxk = 2,
  # the thresholds and the selection rule
  hr.threshold = 1.00, hr.consistency = 1.00, pconsistency.threshold = 0.90,
  stop_threshold = NULL,
  sg_focus = "effMaxSG", selection_rule = "neighborhood", effect_neighborhood = 0.20,
  # selection-adjusted inference
  mr_inference = TRUE,
  mr_inference_args = list(ci_method = "field", draws = 5000L, include_complement = TRUE,
                           field_scale_complement = "selected", field_decompose = TRUE,
                           keep_declaration_field = TRUE,
                           declaration_c0 = c(0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85)),
  parallel_args = list(plan = "sequential")
)

print(fit)
summary(fit)

# Would a screen protecting a uniform benefit (HR 0.70 to 0.85) have declared it?
fs_declaration_calibration(fit, alpha = 0.10, c0 = c(0.70, 0.75, 0.80, 0.85))

Main functions

Function Purpose
forestsearch() Candidate enumeration, screening, selection and (with mr_inference = TRUE) selection-adjusted inference, in one call
fs_mr_inference() Multiplier-resampling inference on a supplied candidate family
fs_declaration_calibration() Family-wise declaration rate of the screen at a protected level, and the calibrated cutoff
mr_estimates_table() The multiplier-resampling estimates in the layout of the bootstrap tables
guohe_algorithm3() The de-biased estimate and one-sided bootstrap bound of Guo and He (2021), for comparison
forestsearch_bootstrap_dofuture(), summarize_bootstrap_results() The full bootstrap bias correction of León et al. (2024)
forestsearch_Kfold(), forestsearch_tenfold(), cv_metrics_tables() Cross-validation of the identification
plot_subgroup_results_forestplot(), plot_sg_weighted_km() Forest plots and weighted Kaplan-Meier curves
generate_aft_dgm_flex(), create_gbsg_dgm(), run_simulation_analysis() Data-generating mechanisms and the simulation framework
mrct_region_sims(), create_dgm_for_mrct() Regional consistency in multi-regional trials

Documentation

  • vignette("forestsearch"): the analysis above, end to end.
  • The package website, https://larry-leon.github.io/forestsearch/, has articles on post-selection inference for the same trial (the full bootstrap beside multiplier resampling), on the binary and continuous analyses of the ACTG 175 trial, on the comparison with Guo and He (2021), on treatment-effect definitions and their causal reading, on the simulation framework, and on the original workflow of León et al. (2024).
  • ?forestsearch documents every argument, with examples on this trial and on the binary and continuous ACTG 175 endpoints.
